meta.title: Nowon Lee — Frontend Engineer
meta.description: Technical profile of frontend engineer Nowon Lee, focused on information accuracy, task visibility, interface responsiveness, and service reliability

identity.name: Nowon Lee
identity.lead: I observe how services behave, trace problems to their causes, and fix them. I want to help make web services easier to use and their information more accurate.
identity.supporting: In TypeScript and React services, I have addressed issues with real-time information, long-running tasks, dashboard data accuracy, and authentication. I continue to check the user experience after deployment.

companies.summary: I handled frontend development for public-sector web services. I improved data accuracy, progress updates for long-running tasks, and deployment reliability, and resolved UI issues caused by API responses.

contributions.title: Fixing incorrect dashboard values and improving transfer efficiency
paragraphs: I fixed missing and incorrect time-series values so dashboard users could accurately check computer resource usage. I aligned metric names and labels with actual responses and corrected ratio calculations. I also traced why separate time series were being combined and updated how they are identified.

I changed queries to fetch only values after the previous request time, reducing data transferred over 10 minutes from 96.5 MB to 41 KB. I compared the deployed dashboard with actual responses to verify the displayed values.

contributions.title: Improving progress updates and status accuracy during long-running document generation
paragraphs: I designed the frontend so users could keep track of the current stage and elapsed time during document generation, which takes 5–10 minutes. I added a confirmation step before leaving the page or canceling generation.

After SSE events, the client checks the server status again so the page reflects the actual state even if events arrive out of order or the connection fails. Status checks stayed at 10 or fewer per task, compared with an estimated 100–200 checks at three-second intervals. After deployment, I verified that generation and cancellation states matched the progress shown on the page.

contributions.title: Eliminating 3–4 second UI freezes and keeping real-time charts continuous
paragraphs: I fixed pages that froze for 3–4 seconds while processing API responses. I moved API requests and response processing into a SharedWorker, used the same approach on run-history and detail pages, and confirmed the fix in the deployed service.

I merged historical values loaded after refresh with new streamed values on the same time basis, keeping the chart continuous without duplicates. I recombined split JSON fragments with the next chunk so real-time updates could continue.

contributions.title: Validating 70+ key flows with consistent authentication recovery
paragraphs: I made more than 70 key authenticated-user flows repeatably testable before release. This coverage surfaced a mismatch between credentials retained in the browser and an expired server session.

I applied the same recovery behavior before users accessed pages that require login and when authentication failed during use, so users received a consistent response. I handled root-cause analysis and deployed the shared recovery behavior to the QA environment.

companies.summary: I made pages reflect user requests immediately, reduced the time it took for the first page to appear, and addressed issues that prevented real-time information from being shown. I documented the loading improvements so other projects could use the same approach.

contributions.title: Showing requested changes immediately and accurately
paragraphs: I made the page respond to user requests immediately, without waiting for a server response. I addressed mismatches between information on the page and server values, and reduced the request count by removing duplicate requests.

contributions.title: Shortening initial load and sharing a reusable setup
paragraphs: I reduced the time it took for pages to become visible to users. I documented the steps so other frontend projects could apply the same improvements.

contributions.title: Restoring real-time information updates
paragraphs: I used Chrome DevTools to find and fix intermittent WebSocket disconnections that stopped real-time information from updating.

contributions.summary: Fixed optional URL parameters incorrectly matching paths that lacked a `/` separator.
contributions.verification: I added tests to check that URLs with a suffix beginning with "." still match as before.

contributions.summary: Fixed an editor defect that prevented Delete or Backspace from removing the final character before an inline image.
contributions.verification: Verified deletion inside and outside tables while preserving regular text deletion.

items.title: AI Agent Workflow
paragraphs: I created rules and skills to help AI agents clarify the work, research what they need, and carry out implementation. Decisions and the reasons for changes remain available when work resumes.
I also built a check for ambiguous Korean wording before documents are saved and used it across multiple repositories.

items.title: Personal Notes Workspace
paragraphs: I started this project because I had to re-enter AI agent instructions and keep adding command notes whenever script parameters changed. Users can select instructions from multiple notes and copy them together, or reuse a command by changing only values such as input filenames.

While using the app myself, I traced and fixed problems that prevented notes from moving to the intended position or batch-copy items from being reordered as expected. I also researched how to design mobile pages to make selecting and reordering text easier.

items.title: Offline Translation Web App
paragraphs: With language models saved ahead of time, users can translate between Korean and English or Korean and Japanese without a network connection and keep entering text on the page while the model runs.
I used browser caching and IndexedDB to store the files and information needed for translation, and automated repeated deployment steps with GitHub Actions.
